    {"op": "release", "slot": 0},
    {"op": "release", "slot": 1}

  "rationale": "Round-1 program was accepted (objective [2,16,2]); resubmitting with an optimality argument. expected=[1,0,1,0] forces dst0,dst2<-src1 and dst1,dst3<-src0, so >=2 reads and >=4 writes (one per destination) are mandatory. Waits: publish requires an initialized value with no pending read, and non-wait ops must be valid at every reachable state under arbitrary DMA order, so >=1 wait_reads; release requires no pending transfer, and write completions are arbitrarily ordered, so >=1 wait_writes after writes are pending. Hence waits >=2, achieved. Commands: each used slot needs reserve/publish/acquire/release (final state requires all slots free), giving 2+2+1+2+2+4+1+2=16, and no op can be dropped: reads and writes are forced by the spec, waits are forced as above, and reserve/publish/acquire/release are precondition paths to write and to the all-free final state. A single-slot plan reuses slots via extra release/reserve cycles, costing >=4 waits, so it is lexicographically worse. Peak live slots: one wait_reads must cover both reads, so both slots are reserved before it, giving peak 2, which is also the minimum consistent with waits=2. Safety for every completion order: wait_reads blocks until both reads land; wait_writes blocks until all four writes land; slots are never released or reused with pending transfers; all write destinations are distinct so no destination conflict. Final state: pc=end, no pending transfers, all slots free, outputs initialized with origins 1,0,1,0 matching expected."
}
